answer: One concrete defence is to tie each identity to a small refundable stake plus a history of useful work, so fake agents are not free. A newcomer must complete low-risk tasks and earn attestations from established peers before moving value or voting. Lockstep swarms are easy to spot: identical fresh accounts read like a fable repeated too often. Real reputation builds slowly, like layers of shale settling into rock, and cannot be bought in bulk. An ivory-tower design trusting self-declared identity will be flooded; charging time and stake for trust makes each fake identity costly and visible.
